title: Paddy Nitrogen and Zinc Deficiency Management
content: Yellowing of older lower leaves in paddy typically indicates nitrogen deficiency, whereas rusty brown spots or chlorosis on younger leaves indicates zinc deficiency (Khaira disease). Farmers should verify water levels, inspect root health for sulphide toxicity or root rot, and apply recommended top-dressing of urea in split doses or zinc sulphate (0.5% foliar spray with lime) if zinc deficiency is diagnosed.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad & UAS Bangalore Package of Practices

title: Paddy Yellow Stem Borer Management
content: Yellow Stem Borer larvae bore into the central tiller causing dead hearts during vegetative stage and white ears (white heads) at heading stage. Management includes clipping seedling leaf tips before transplanting, setting up pheromone traps @ 5/acre, conserving natural parasitoids like Trichogramma, and applying recommended threshold-based chemical granules like Cartap hydrochloride 4G or Chlorantraniliprole when pest pressure exceeds economic threshold.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) - Integrated Pest Management Guidelines

title: Ragi Moisture Stress and Drought Management
content: During prolonged dry spells or delayed rainfall, ragi (finger millet) crops exhibit leaf curling, premature drying, and wilting. Protective measures include providing protective life-saving irrigation at tillering or flowering stages if water is available, spraying 1% potassium chloride (KCl) or 2% urea to reduce transpiration shock, maintaining inter-cultivation soil mulching to conserve root zone moisture, and practicing clean weeding to eliminate moisture competition.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Bangalore - Dryland Agriculture Technical Bulletin

title: Ragi Blast Disease (Pyricularia grisea) Management
content: Ragi blast affects leaves (spindle-shaped lesions with grey centers), nodes (blackened rotting), and neck/fingers (grain sterility). Management involves using resistant cultivars (like GPU-28, ML-365), treating seeds with Carbendazim (2g/kg seed), avoiding excess nitrogen fertilization, and applying preventive sprays of Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6g/L) or Mancozeb if weather is overcast with high humidity.
source: All India Coordinated Research Project on Small Millets (AICRP-ICAR), Bengaluru

title: Maize Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) Management
content: Fall Armyworm causes characteristic ragged pinholes, windowing on leaves, and heavy fecal frass inside the central whorl. Management includes deep summer ploughing, installing pheromone traps @ 4/acre for monitoring, handpicking egg masses, applying Neem oil (Azadirachtin 1500 ppm @ 5ml/L) or Metarhizium anisopliae early, and whorl application of Emamectin benzoate 5% SG (0.4g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (0.4ml/L) during severe early-to-mid whorl stages.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana & ICAR-NBAIR Bengaluru

title: Maize Waterlogging and Excess Rainfall Management
content: Maize is highly sensitive to waterlogging, especially in seedling and knee-high stages. Prolonged standing water causes root asphyxiation, nutrient leaching, and stunting. Farmers must dig drainage furrows immediately to remove stagnant water, apply a foliar spray of 1-2% urea or DAP once field drains to stimulate root recovery, and inspect for secondary bacterial stalk rot infections.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) - Agronomy Advisory

title: Groundnut Tikka Leaf Spot Management
content: Tikka leaf spot (Cercospora arachidicola / Cercosporidium personatum) produces dark brown-to-black circular spots with yellow halos on older leaves, leading to severe defoliation. Recommended practices include crop rotation, seed treatment with Trichoderma viride or Thiram (3g/kg), and foliar application of Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Carbendazim (1g/L) or Hexaconazole (1ml/L) at the onset of spot appearance.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR), Junagadh

title: Groundnut White Grub Management
content: White grub (Holotrichia consanguinea) larvae feed on rootlets and pod pegs, causing patchy wilting and sudden drying of standing groundnut plants. Management involves light trap catches of adult beetles after monsoon showers, seed treatment with Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (2ml/kg), application of well-decomposed FYM (avoiding raw manure), and soil drenching with Chlorpyrifos 20 EC if grub attack is identified in active patches.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad - Oilseeds Advisory

title: Sugarcane Early Shoot Borer Management
content: Early Shoot Borer (Chilo infuscatellus) attacks 1-3 month old cane shoots producing central dead hearts that pull out easily with an unpleasant odour. Management involves trash mulching @ 3 tonnes/acre in cane rows, earthing-up operations at 45 days, releasing Trichogramma chilonis egg parasitoids, and soil application of Cartap hydrochloride 4G or Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR along the rows before irrigation.
source: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore

title: Sugarcane Red Rot Disease Prevention
content: Red rot (Colletotrichum falcatum) causes yellowing and drying of the third or fourth leaf from crown, longitudinal reddening of internal stalk tissues with crosswise white patches, and sour alcoholic smell. Control relies strictly on planting certified disease-free sets, practicing set treatment with Carbendazim (0.1%) hot water treatment, burning infected stubbles, maintaining crop rotation with rice, and avoiding flood irrigation from infected plots.
source: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore

title: Cotton Pink Bollworm and Sucking Pest Management
content: Pink bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) damages squares and bolls, leading to rosetted flowers and stained lint. Sucking pests (thrips, aphids, jassids) cause leaf crinkling and curling. Integrated control includes pheromone trapping @ 8-10/acre, destruction of rosette flowers, conserving predatory ladybird beetles, installing yellow/blue sticky traps, and rotating insecticides (Neem formulations, Flonicamid 50 WG, or Spinetoram 11.7 SC) when thresholds are crossed.
source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur

title: Cotton Waterlogging Reddening and Foliar Nutrition
content: Excess rainfall and prolonged soil saturation cause cotton leaf yellowing, bronzing/reddening, and square shedding due to poor nitrogen and magnesium uptake. Immediate field drainage is necessary. After water recedes, spray 1% Magnesium Sulphate (MgSO4) + 1% Urea or 19:19:19 balanced fertilizer at 10-day intervals to restore chlorophyll synthesis and retain fruiting branches.
source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur - Crop Advisory

title: Chilli Leaf Curl and Thrips/Mites Management
content: Chilli leaf curling is predominantly caused by Thrips (leaves curl upwards with boat-shaped appearance) or Mites (leaves curl downwards with elongation). Control includes erecting blue sticky traps for thrips and yellow sticky traps for whiteflies @ 15/acre, spraying neem cake extract or Pongamia oil, and applying targeted acaricides/insecticides like Diafenthiuron 50 WP (1g/L), Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (1ml/L), or Fipronil 5 SC (1.5ml/L).
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: Chilli Anthracnose and Die-Back Disease Management
content: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum capsici) causes tip die-back on twigs and circular sunken necrotic lesions on ripening fruits. Recommended management includes using disease-free treated seed, avoiding overhead sprinkler irrigation, prompt removal of infected fruit, and foliar spraying of Azoxystrobin 23 SC (1ml/L) or Copper oxychloride (2.5g/L) + Streptocycline during humid conditions.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: Onion Excess Rain Drainage and Purple Blotch Control
content: Excessive rainfall in onion fields leads to root suffocation, bulb rotting, and outbreaks of Purple Blotch (Alternaria porri - water-soaked lesions that turn purplish-brown). Action steps: create immediate shallow exit drains to remove standing water, avoid applying additional nitrogen until soils dry, and spray Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5g/L) or Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) combined with an agricultural sticker/spreader.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR), Pune

title: Onion Thrips (Thrips tabaci) Management
content: Onion thrips lacerate leaf tissues causing silvery white blotches and distorted curly leaf tips. Severe infestation leads to leaf drying and undersized bulb development. Management includes installing blue sticky traps @ 20/acre, sprinkler irrigation to dislodge nymphs, and spraying Profenofos 50 EC (1ml/L) or Spinosad 45 SC (0.3ml/L) directed into the leaf sheaths.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR), Pune

title: Potato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) Management
content: Late blight appears as water-soaked irregular dark brown lesions on leaf margins with white fuzzy fungal growth on leaf undersides in cold, humid weather. Rapid destruction of foliage can occur. Management requires using certified disease-free seed tubers, earthing-up to prevent tuber infection, and spraying preventive Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5g/L) followed by systemic Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Dimethomorph (1g/L) if active lesions appear.
source: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI), Shimla

title: Potato Tuber Bulking and Balanced Nutrition
content: Potato requires balanced nitrogen, phosphorus, and high potassium during the tuber bulking stage (45-70 days after planting). Excessive late nitrogen causes foliage overgrown at the expense of tuber formation. Adequate potassium (SOP/MOP) improves tuber size, starch content, and drought resistance. Ensure uniform light irrigations and avoid alternate wetting and severe drying cycles.
source: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI), Shimla

title: Banana Potassium Deficiency and Leaf Yellowing
content: Potassium deficiency in banana is characterized by rapid yellowing of older leaf tips and margins (orange-yellow chlorosis) that curls backward and rapidly dries, while the midrib stays green. Ensure application of recommended Muriate of Potash (MOP) in 3-4 split doses during vegetative and bunch development stages, and apply organic compost to enhance potassium uptake.
source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB), Tiruchirappalli

title: Banana Panama Wilt and Sigatoka Leaf Spot
content: Panama disease (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense) causes yellowing of lower leaves along margins, petiole buckling, and longitudinal splitting of the pseudostem base. Sigatoka leaf spot causes oval spindle-shaped dark brown spots with grey centers. Management includes using tissue-cultured suckers, soil application of Trichoderma viride with neem cake, eliminating infected plants, and foliar spray of Propiconazole (1ml/L) with sticker for Sigatoka control.
source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB), Tiruchirappalli

title: Tomato Early Blight and Yellow Leaf Management
content: Yellowing of lower leaves in tomato with concentric target-board dark rings indicates Early Blight (Alternaria solani). General chlorosis without spots may indicate nitrogen shortage or root-knot nematode damage. Farmers should stake plants, practice bottom-leaf pruning to improve air circulation, avoid splash watering, and apply copper oxychloride (2.5g/L) or Mancozeb (2g/L) as protective spray.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: Sorghum Shoot Fly (Atherigona soccata) Management
content: Sorghum shoot fly attacks 1 to 4 week old seedlings causing drying of the central shoot (dead heart) that produces tiny side tillers. Management involves early sowing within 7-10 days of monsoon onset, seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70 WS (3g/kg seed) or Thiamethoxam 30 FS (10ml/kg), setting up fishmeal traps @ 10/ha to attract and kill adult flies, and foliar application of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (0.3ml/L) if dead hearts exceed 10% in young seedlings.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (IIMR), Hyderabad & UAS Dharwad Package of Practices

title: Sorghum Charcoal Rot and Post-Flowering Drought Stress
content: Charcoal rot (Macrophomina phaseolina) is severe in Rabi sorghum during post-flowering soil moisture stress. Symptoms include premature drying of lower leaves, soft lodging of stalks, and internal disintegration of pith with numerous black microsclerotia. Control relies on growing drought-tolerant cultivars (CSV-29R, M35-1), providing one protective irrigation during grain filling stage if possible, balanced potassium application, and avoiding excessive plant density in dry soils.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad - Dryland Agriculture Technical Bulletin

title: Pearl Millet Downy Mildew (Green Ear Disease) Management
content: Downy mildew (Sclerospora graminicola) causes pale yellow chlorotic streaks on leaves and transforms floral heads into green leafy structures (green ear), causing total grain loss. Recommended management: plant resistant hybrids (GHB-538, ICTP-8203), treat seeds with Metalaxyl-M (Apron XL @ 2g/kg seed), rogue out and bury infected chlorotic plants before 30 days of sowing, and spray Metalaxyl 35 WS (2g/L) if systemic infection appears on young foliage.
source: All India Coordinated Research Project on Pearl Millet (AICRP-ICAR) & UAS Raichur

title: Pearl Millet Moisture Conservation and Inter-cropping in Drylands
content: In northern dry zones of Karnataka with shallow red and black soils, pearl millet provides high drought tolerance. Recommended practices: sow in paired rows (30/60 cm) intercropped with red gram or cowpea (2:1 ratio) to maximize rainfall utilization, carry out inter-cultivation with blade harrows at 20 and 35 days after sowing to create a dust mulch, and apply 25 kg N + 25 kg P2O5/ha as basal with remaining N top-dressed after rain.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Raichur - Package of Practices for Dryland Agriculture

title: Red Gram Pod Borer (Helicoverpa armigera) Management
content: Gram pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera) caterpillars feed on floral buds, flowers, and bore into developing pods creating circular holes and devouring seeds. Control: install pheromone traps @ 4/acre for monitoring, shake plants over plastic sheets to dislodge early larvae, spray HaNPV 250 LE/acre with jaggery (10g/L) at evening, and apply Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (0.3ml/L) or Emamectin benzoate 5 SG (0.4g/L) at 50% flowering and early pod set.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR) & UAS Raichur (Kalaburagi Red Gram Research Station)

title: Red Gram Fusarium Wilt and Sterility Mosaic Management
content: Fusarium wilt (Fusarium udum) causes progressive drooping of leaves, interveinal chlorosis, and dark purple-black vascular browning inside split stems. Sterility mosaic causes bushy pale leaves with no pod setting. Management: grow wilt-resistant varieties (BSMR-736, GRG-811, TS-3R), treat seeds with Trichoderma viride (10g/kg) or Carbendazim (2g/kg), practice crop rotation with sorghum or maize, and spray Fenazaquin 10 EC (1ml/L) to control sterility mosaic mite vectors.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Raichur - Pulse Research Station Kalaburagi

title: Bengal Gram (Chickpea) Fusarium Wilt Management
content: Chickpea wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceris) causes drooping of petioles, greyish-green foliage fading to straw-yellow, and dark brown xylem discoloration in tap roots. Management: plant wilt-resistant cultivars (JG-11, JAKI-9218, BGD-103), treat seed with Trichoderma harzianum (4g/kg) + Carbendazim (1g/kg), perform deep summer ploughing to destroy pathogen inoculum, avoid sowing in poorly drained black soils, and follow 3-year crop rotation.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad - Pulses Advisory

title: Bengal Gram Pod Borer Management and Nipping
content: Pod borer (Helicoverpa) larvae feed on foliage and bore into pods during pod filling stage. Cultural control: apical shoot nipping at 30-40 days after sowing stimulates profuse branching and removes early egg batches. Install bird perches (T-shaped @ 20/acre) and pheromone traps @ 5/acre. If larval count exceeds 1 per meter row, spray NSKE 5% followed by Indoxacarb 14.5 SC (0.5ml/L) or Flubendiamide 39.35 SC (0.2ml/L).
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Regional Station & UAS Dharwad

title: Green Gram Yellow Mosaic Virus and Powdery Mildew Management
content: Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV) transmitted by whiteflies produces irregular bright yellow patches that coalesce into total leaf yellowing and pod distortion. Powdery mildew causes white talcum powder-like fungal coating on leaves. Management: use MYMV-tolerant cultivars (DGGV-2, BGS-9), seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70 WS (3ml/kg), install yellow sticky traps @ 10/acre, and spray Wettable Sulphur 80 WP (3g/L) or Hexaconazole 5 EC (1ml/L) for powdery mildew.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad - Department of Plant Pathology

title: Black Gram Powdery Mildew and Leaf Crinkle Management
content: Powdery mildew (Erysiphe polygoni) in black gram causes white floury patches on leaves and pods, reducing grain size and quality. Leaf crinkle virus causes crinkling, thickening, and dark green puckering of leaves. Management: sow certified resistant seeds (LBG-752, Rashmi), treat seeds with Thiamethoxam 30 FS (4ml/kg), and spray Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or Carbendazim (1g/L) at first symptom of white powdery patches.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Bangalore - Pulses Advisory Bulletin

title: Sunflower Alternaria Leaf Blight and Head Rot Management
content: Alternaria blight (Alternaria helianthi) causes dark brown circular spots with concentric rings on leaves and flower bracts. Rhizopus head rot causes soft rotting and shedding of mature seed heads following rains. Control measures: seed treatment with Thiram or Captan (3g/kg), maintain 60x30 cm spacing, and spray Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) or Zineb (2g/L) at 35, 50, and 65 days after sowing. Ensure good drainage to prevent head rot.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research (IIOR) & UAS Raichur

title: Soybean Asian Rust and Stem Fly Management
content: Soybean rust (Phakopsora pachyrhizi) produces tiny tan pustules on leaf undersides causing premature drying and defoliation during humid Kharif. Stem fly (Melanagromyza sojae) maggots mine into the stem causing wilting. Management: sow rust-tolerant varieties (DSb-21, JS-335), seed treatment with Thiamethoxam 30 FS (10ml/kg), and apply prophylactic spray of Hexaconazole 5 EC (1ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (1.25ml/L) upon overcast rain alerts.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR) & UAS Dharwad

title: Turmeric Rhizome Rot and Leaf Blotch Management
content: Rhizome rot (Pythium aphanidermatum) causes water-soaking at pseudo-stem collars, foul decaying smell, and leaf yellowing drying from tip downwards. Leaf blotch (Taphrina maculans) produces small rectangular yellow-brown spots. Management: use disease-free seed rhizomes, dip in Trichoderma viride (10g/L) + Mancozeb (2g/L) for 30 minutes before planting, ensure raised bed planting with drainage trenches, and drench soil with Metalaxyl-Mancozeb (2g/L) around affected clumps.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR), Kozhikode & UAS Bangalore

title: Ginger Soft Rot (Pythium) and Bacterial Wilt Management
content: Soft rot (Pythium spp.) and Bacterial wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) cause massive rotting of ginger rhizomes in Malnad and Coastal Karnataka. Symptoms include marginal leaf yellowing, water-soaked stem bases that pull out easily, and bacterial oozing. Control: strictly plant certified disease-free rhizomes, practice solarization of nursery beds, provide shade and raised-bed drainage, apply Trichoderma-enriched neem cake (500kg/acre), and soil drench with Copper oxychloride (3g/L) or Streptocycline (0.2g/L).
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR) & UHS Bagalkot (KRC College of Horticulture, Arabhavi)

title: Black Pepper Quick Wilt (Phytophthora Foot Rot) Management
content: Quick wilt (Phytophthora capsici) infects roots and collar of black pepper vines causing sudden blackening and dropping of green leaves and total vine collapse within 2 weeks during monsoon in Kodagu and Chikkamagaluru. Control: clear weed growth around vine basins, paint Bordeaux paste on lower stem up to 1 meter, apply Trichoderma viride with FYM in May-June, and spray 1% Bordeaux mixture or Potassium phosphonate (3ml/L) pre-monsoon and post-monsoon.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR) Regional Station, Appangala, Kodagu

title: Cardamom Katte Mosaic Disease and Thrips Management
content: Katte mosaic virus transmitted by banana aphids produces discontinuous chlorotic stripes on young leaves, severe stunting, and poor flowering. Thrips (Sciothrips cardamomi) lacerate capsules causing scabby warty encrustations (chanka). Management: rogue out and incinerate Katte-infected clumps promptly, maintain uniform shade trees, spray Quinalphos 25 EC (2ml/L) or Spinosad 45 SC (0.3ml/L) on panicles during flowering to protect developing capsules.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR) Research Centre, Appangala, Kodagu

title: Brinjal Shoot and Fruit Borer (Leucinodes orbonalis) Management
content: Shoot and fruit borer larvae bore into terminal shoots causing drooping and drying of tips, and bore into developing fruits leaving holes filled with frass. Management includes regular clipping and burning of wilted shoots with larvae inside, installing pheromone traps @ 12/acre (Lucin-lure), spraying Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%), and applying Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (0.4ml/L) or Emamectin benzoate 5 SG (0.4g/L) during active fruiting.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Hesaraghatta, Bengaluru

title: Cabbage Diamondback Moth (DBM) and Black Rot Management
content: Diamondback moth (Plutella xylostella) larvae feed on leaf undersides creating transparent window patches and head boreholes. Black rot (Xanthomonas) causes V-shaped yellow necrotic lesions along leaf margins. Integrated control: plant mustard trap crop (2 rows of mustard for every 25 rows of cabbage), spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt @ 1g/L) or Spinetoram (0.9ml/L) for DBM, and spray Streptocycline (0.1g/L) + Copper oxychloride (2g/L) for black rot.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: Bhendi Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus and Fruit Borer Management
content: Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus (YVMV) transmitted by whiteflies causes bright yellow vein network clearing, leaf thickening, and stunted chlorotic fruit. Fruit borers (Earias spp.) bore into shoots and pods. Management: grow resistant varieties (Arka Anamika, Arka Abhay), install yellow sticky traps @ 10/acre, spray Neem oil (3ml/L) or Imidacloprid (0.3ml/L) for whitefly control, and spray Spinosad 45 SC (0.3ml/L) for fruit borer control.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: Mango Hopper, Powdery Mildew, and Fruit Fly Management
content: Mango hoppers (Idioscopus spp.) suck sap from flowering panicles causing blossom withering and sooty mold from honeydew secretions. Powdery mildew causes white powdery coating on flowers. Fruit flies lay eggs inside ripening fruits causing pulp decay. Control: spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.3ml/L) + Wettable Sulphur (2g/L) at bud burst stage, install Methyl eugenol pheromone traps @ 4/acre for male fruit flies, and collect and bury fallen fruits.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Hesaraghatta, Bengaluru

title: Pomegranate Bacterial Blight (Telya / Xanthomonas) Management
content: Bacterial blight (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. punicae) causes dark brown water-soaked angular spots on leaves, stem cankers, and characteristic dark L- or Y-shaped cracking on developing fruits in northern Karnataka dry zones. Management involves orchard sanitation, pruning infected twigs in dry spell followed by Bordeaux paste application, and protective sprays of Copper hydroxide 53.8 DF (2g/L) + 2-Bromo-2-nitropropane-1,3-diol (Bacteromycin @ 0.5g/L) at 10-15 day intervals during monsoon.
source: ICAR-National Research Centre on Pomegranate (NRCP), Solapur & UAS Raichur

title: Grapes Downy Mildew and Powdery Mildew Management
content: Downy mildew (Plasmopara viticola) causes yellowish oily spots on upper leaf surfaces and dense white downy cottony fungal growth underneath, leading to fruit cluster rot. Powdery mildew causes ash-grey powdery coating on berries resulting in berry cracking. Control: maintain canopy openness through shoot thinning, apply prophylactic sprays of 1% Bordeaux mixture or Mancozeb (2g/L), and spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Azoxystrobin (1ml/L) upon downy mildew outbreak.
source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Grapes (NRCG), Pune & ICAR-IIHR Bengaluru

title: Papaya Ringspot Virus (PRSV) and Fruit Rot Management
content: Papaya Ringspot Virus (PRSV) transmitted by aphids causes leaf mottling, blistering, shoe-stringing, dark green water-soaked oily streaks on petioles, and concentric rings on fruits. Anthracnose causes sunken circular rotting spots on ripe fruits. Management: plant tolerant cultivars (Red Lady), plant 2-3 border rows of maize or sorghum to trap aphids, destroy severely virus-infected plants, and spray Carbendazim (1g/L) or Azoxystrobin (1ml/L) for fruit rot control.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: Acid Lime Citrus Canker and Gummosis Management
content: Citrus canker (Xanthomonas citri) causes raised corky crater-like scabby brown lesions with yellow chlorotic halos on leaves, twigs, and fruits, leading to heavy fruit dropping (prevalent in Vijayapura lime belt). Gummosis (Phytophthora) causes trunk bark splitting and gum exudation. Control: prune canker-affected twigs before monsoon and spray Copper oxychloride (3g/L) + Streptocycline (0.1g/L) at 15-day intervals during new leaf flushes. Paint tree trunks with Bordeaux paste.
source: University of Horticultural Sciences (UHS), Bagalkot & ICAR-CCRI

title: Arecanut Koleroga (Mahali / Fruit Rot) Management
content: Koleroga or Mahali (Phytophthora meadii) causes dark green water-soaked lesions on nut bases, resulting in massive dropping of immature green nuts and rotting of fruit bunches during continuous heavy monsoon in Malnad and Coastal Karnataka. Control involves cleaning palm crowns before monsoon, covering developing nut bunches with 100-gauge polythene covers before heavy showers, and applying prophylactic spraying of 1% Bordeaux mixture before monsoon onset and a second spray 40 days later.
source: ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI) Regional Station, Vittal, Dakshina Kannada

title: Arecanut Yellow Leaf Disease and Root Grub Management
content: Yellow Leaf Disease (YLD) caused by phytoplasma causes progressive yellowing of inner leaflets starting from tips, kernel blackening, and gradual crown reduction. Root grubs feed on roots causing palm loosening and yellowing. Management: apply balanced NPK + magnesium sulphate (100g/palm), provide organic green manuring with Glyricidia, improve drainage in low-lying valleys, and drench soil with Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (5ml/L) for root grubs.
source: ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Kasaragod & UAS Bangalore

title: Coconut Rhinoceros Beetle, Red Palm Weevil, and Bud Rot Management
content: Rhinoceros beetle (Oryctes rhinoceros) bores into unopened fronds causing characteristic V-shaped geometric cuts on leaves. Bud rot (Phytophthora) rots the central cabbage spindle. Control: hook out adult beetles from crowns, fill top leaf axils with sevidol or neem cake mixed with sand (1:2), install pheromone traps (Ferrolure+ / Rhinolure), and apply 1% Bordeaux paste to bud rot affected crown after cleaning rotted tissues.
source: ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Kasaragod & UAS Bangalore

title: Coffee Leaf Rust (Hemileia vastatrix) and White Stem Borer Management
content: Coffee Leaf Rust causes circular orange-yellow powdery pustules on the lower leaf surface, resulting in severe defoliation and berry drop in Arabica coffee. White stem borer (Xylotrechus quadripes) larvae bore into main stems causing stem ridges, wilting, and palm death. Management: apply 0.5% Bordeaux mixture spray (pre-monsoon in May and post-monsoon in October), trace and uproot borer-infested bushes before flight periods, and maintain optimal two-tier shade.
source: Central Coffee Research Institute (CCRI), Coffee Board of India, Balehonnur, Chikkamagaluru

title: Cashew Tea Mosquito Bug and Stem Borer Management
content: Tea Mosquito Bug (Helopeltis antonii) nymphs and adults suck sap from tender shoots, panicles, and developing nuts, causing dark necrotic lesions and blossom blight in coastal Karnataka. Cashew stem and root borer (CSRB) grubs tunnel into trunk bark with frass extrusion. Management: spray Lambda cyhalothrin 5 EC (0.6ml/L) or Acetamiprid 20 SP (0.5g/L) at flushing, flowering, and nut formation stages, and swab tree trunks with Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (2ml/L) for stem borers.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Cashew Research (DCR), Puttur, Dakshina Kannada

title: FCV Tobacco Frog Eye Leaf Spot and Caterpillar Management
content: Frog eye leaf spot (Cercospora nicotianae) produces small circular parchment-like spots with white centers and dark brown margins on mature tobacco leaves in Mysuru and Hunsur light soils. Tobacco caterpillar (Spodoptera litura) defoliates seedlings. Management: practice proper crop rotation, avoid excess nitrogen, remove lower sand leaves at harvest, spray Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) for leaf spots, and use pheromone traps for caterpillar monitoring.
source: ICAR-Central Tobacco Research Institute (CTRI) Research Station, Hunsur, Mysuru

title: Jasmine Leaf Webworm, Bud Borer, and Blossom Blight Management
content: Leaf webworm (Glyphodes pulverulentalis) webs leaves together and feeds inside, while Bud borer (Hendecasis duplifascialis) bores into floral buds making holes and discoloring petals in Mysore and Udupi Mallige. Blossom blight (Alternaria) rots flower buds during humid weather. Management: prune bushes in November-December, collect and burn webbed shoots, spray Novaluron 10 EC (1ml/L) or Spinosad (0.3ml/L) at bud initiation, and apply Mancozeb (2g/L) for blossom blight.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru & Department of Horticulture, Karnataka

title: Marigold Alternaria Leaf Spot and Bud Borer Management
content: Leaf spot and flower blight (Alternaria tagetica) cause brown circular necrotic spots on leaves and premature rotting of flower heads. Bud borer (Helicoverpa armigera) eats holes in opening flower buds. Management: treat seeds with Trichoderma (4g/kg), maintain adequate spacing (60x45 cm), spray Mancozeb (2g/L) or Iprodione (1.5g/L) at 10-day intervals upon spot emergence, and apply Emamectin benzoate (0.4g/L) for bud borer.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: General Field Drainage and Post-Flood Crop Care
content: Excess rainfall and prolonged standing water deplete soil oxygen, weaken root hairs, and promote root-rotting fungi (Pythium, Phytophthora). Essential remedial steps: 1) Open main and lateral drainage trenches immediately. 2) Avoid heavy machine entry on wet soil to prevent compaction. 3) Once soil reaches working moisture, aerate the surface by light hoeing. 4) Apply light foliar micronutrients and avoid heavy basal fertilizer until fresh roots emerge.
source: Karnataka State Department of Agriculture (KSDA) & ICAR Advisory
